checks.claim: Chain measure, mass and source convention: n ordered factors G(s_{j+1}-s_j), s_{n+1}=t, no initial G(s_1), and mass t^(2n)/(2n)!, including the d3 sphere measure.
checks.reason: The recursion f_n(t)=int_0^t (t-r) f_{n-1}(r) dr with f_0=1 gives t^2/2 and t^4/24 at the first two orders and the stated formula in general. The chain matches author (2.15)-(2.16) on p.10. Mass and support match (2.4)-(2.5) on p.7, and the unit-time dilation matches (2.6).

checks.claim: Bochner construction, covariance bound and stochastic Fubini at fixed positive rho.
checks.reason: C_rho=K_eta(s-r)Gamma_(2eps)(z-w) is the equal-width case of E:source-joint-covariance. It is nonnegative, and Gaussian Cauchy-Schwarz bounds it by the finite K_eta(0)Gamma_(2eps)(0). Holder and scalar Gaussian moments bound products in L2 uniformly over vertices, so L2 continuity and the finite chain measure give the Bochner integral and exchange.

checks.claim: Green smoothing is removed before noise by the square/cross weak-limit argument, and the actual unmasked integral inherits q_n from L:vertex-crude.
checks.reason: Heat-smoothed Green measures converge weakly with masses preserved. The covariance products are bounded and spatially continuous, and the chain mass supplies the time majorant, so both square moments and the cross moment converge to one sum and L2 convergence follows. This matches the convention in canonical lines 669-678, and L:vertex-crude depends only on the law. The note on 'These are the canonical...' wording is in minor findings.

checks.claim: All diagrams are handled and the mask comparison is correct: unequal, empty, self and cross diagrams, odd zero, and one physical mask at every vertex after regularization.
checks.reason: The Wick formula (2.19) on p.12 uses all pair partitions. Each pair-partition integrand is nonnegative. Masking multiplies it by prod_i m(z_i) in [0,1], one factor per vertex independent of partner or chain. E:masked-order-comparison and E:masked-order-bound follow, including n=k=0. The text asserts only diagramwise expected-displacement order, with no samplewise, PSD or nonlinear covariance comparison.

checks.claim: Cone Picard, uniqueness and L2/pathwise identification hold without global source supremum moments.
checks.reason: A sample bound M on the compact backward cone gives M^n T^(2n)/(2n)! for each term and B M^n T^(2n)/(2n)! for the iterated difference. Ordinary Fubini identifies each Bochner term with the pathwise chain integral at a fixed terminal point over countably many orders. An almost surely convergent L2 subsequence identifies the sum. No common event over widths is used.

checks.claim: Two-point and positive-average comparison, with stationarity only for the unmasked solution.
checks.reason: Sigma q_n q_k gives L1 convergence of products and passes the termwise comparison to E:masked-two-point. Stationarity of the unmasked Picard integrals and Cauchy-Schwarz give E[u_rho(t,x)u_rho(t,y)]<=E|u_rho(t,0)|^2. L2 continuity in x and the bound Q_t give the Bochner average, and absolute Fubini gives E:masked-average-source. Masked stationarity is expressly not used.

checks.claim: Terminal reversal, pairing bijection and the full canonical moment limit at arbitrary rates.
checks.reason: The reversal s'_j=t-s_{n+1-j}, z'_j=-z_{n+1-j} on two chains with common (t,0) preserves pair differences up to sign, and evenness absorbs the sign. The relabeling agrees with the explicit involution rho in P:mixed. L:joint-fixed-order gives finite diagram limits, including empty chains. The finite-square argument with the q_n q_k majorant gives E:masked-unmasked-moment-limit. The relabeling map r is implicit, as noted in minor findings.

The premise is discharged only in P:constant-raw-average, by E:constant-tested-limit. The dependency is not circular, because the Young construction does not use the canonical moment transfer.

checks.claim: Phase F: continuous injective embedding, constants in neither Sobolev entry, closed proper iE, and boundedness of L_psi with both columns.
checks.reason: The bound ||f||_{L2(B_eps)} eps^(d/2) ||phi||_2 tends to 0 while delta_0 gives 1, which excludes constants from every H^sigma and gives injectivity. Duality and test integrals give continuity. The direct sum gives completeness, separability and the closed proper non-dense inclusion. The Peetre inequality and the c_d convolution kernel give boundedness on H^(+/-1/2), and psi is in both Sobolev entries.

checks.claim: Free group and total finite propagation: unitary c_d factor, compact kernel matrix, masses 1,t,0,1, and local E/constant cancellation.
checks.reason: Ghat=c_d sin(t|xi|)/|xi| gives the convolution multiplier sin(t|xi|)/|xi|, and the other entries give cos and -|xi| sin, matching E:variance-free-matrix and author (2.3). Transpose continuity and Schwartz density extend the identity to E. Pairing the entries with 1 gives exactly c1+t c2 and c2. Supports lie in B_|t|, so vanishing total data on an enlarged ball propagates even when the summands cancel. Operator-norm continuity is not claimed.

checks.claim: Actual driver: same raw A_j, both localizations, psi-independence, Ai=iM_E, both columns, compactness, source limit and raw W-measurability.
checks.reason: L:driver-gain-localization holds termwise, P:source-gaussian-transfer uses the same A_j, and bounded D_chi passes the identity through almost surely uniform limits. Since chi(psi-psi')=0, right localization kills the psi difference, and chi psi=chi gives Ai=iM_E. The columns are iM_E(psi,0) and iM_E(0,psi). Bounded composition transfers compactness and E:source-driver-limit. A is a deterministic transform of the W-measurable M_R, while the source may use J.

checks.reason: E:source-transfer-norm with C=1 and ||L_psi|| gives a uniform sqrt(p) bound. E X^(2n)<=C^(2n)(2n)^n and n!>=(n/e)^n give a geometric series when 2ecC^2<1, uniformly in rho.

E_{j+1}<=2E_j+2^(j+2)Lambda closes to E_j<=2^j E_0+j 2^(j+1)Lambda. Both seminorms <=K fix a common ell. The piece count is uniform in the start. ||U-I||<=1/3 gives Neumann invertibility. Local-ball stability plus uniform tails gives convergence in probability without a random Lipschitz claim. 1/theta<2 and pC(1+x)^q<=cx^2+C_{p,c} give uniform moments and UI. pi_C of Riemann sums and closedness give E:constant-flow-range. S_F(t)iS(-r)=S_F(t-r)i and S_F(t)e_0=e_0 give Duhamel. The induction bound and Duhamel norm C_T B_T T identify the sum by uniqueness. B_F(b)W_{n-1}=(0,bX_{n-1}), and testing against compact phi with majorant ||phi||_inf||f_r||_1(t-r) gives X_n with positive measures, including the d3 sphere. Iteration gives X_{rho,n}^m.
